name: schedule_task
description: Create, list, update, or cancel scheduled Jarvis tasks. Use when the user wants Jarvis to run a future one-time or recurring query or workflow like daily status reports, periodic checks, or scheduled emails. Supports natural schedule phrases like 'tomorrow at 1pm', 'April 4th at 4pm', '4/4 at 4pm', '04/04/2026 at 4pm', 'every day at 10am', 'every weekday at 9am', and 'every 6 hours'.

action.description: What to do: create, list, update, cancel, permanently delete, queue an immediate run, or inspect recent run history.

task_id.description: Required for update, cancel, delete, run_now, and list_runs.

task_type.description: Task type for create. Use query for natural language tasks or workflow for deterministic workflows.

query.description: Natural language Jarvis query to run later. Required when task_type=query.

workflow_id.description: Workflow ID to run. Required when task_type=workflow.

when.description: Natural schedule expression like 'tomorrow at 1pm', 'April 4th at 4pm', '4/4 at 4pm', '04/04/2026 at 4pm', 'every day at 10am', 'every weekday at 9am', 'every Wednesday at 2pm', or 'every 6 hours'.

timezone.description: Optional IANA timezone like 'America/Los_Angeles'. Defaults to JARVIS_TIMEZONE.

mode.description: Execution mode for the future task. Defaults to cloud.

allow_overlap.description: If true, the task may start even if a previous run is still active.

max_retries.description: Maximum retry attempts if a run fails.

status.description: For list action: filter by enabled state.

limit.description: For list and list_runs: maximum number of items to return.
